summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, EBITDA up 45.6% to INR54.59 crores at a 20.6% margin, with the order book at a record INR174 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, below management's earlier 20-25% target, because supplies on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR were deferred by buyers. Profitability improved sharply: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps to 20.6%, PAT rose 67.2% to INR30.14 crores, and Q4 EBITDA margin crossed 21%. The company deployed about INR27 crores of capex in FY26 under a Board-approved INR100 crores programme spanning FY26-FY28, and entered aluminium windows and facade with INR56 crores of orders. Working capital rose as management paid suppliers early and stocked PVC resin and polymers ahead of West Asia-related price increases.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it will not reach 0.75
Record high; vs INR120-140 crores last year

segments.name: PVC/UPVC polymer products
segments.commentary: Management said about 84% of FY26 revenue (about INR220 crores) came from PVC and UPVC, of which about INR60 crores was UPVC windows and the rest PVC profiles. EBITDA margin in this segment was higher than modular; PBT margin was about 16.6%.

segments.name: Modular furniture (Dynasty)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR43 crores (about 16% of sales), with PBT margin around 9%, which management said was up about 80% YoY. Four new builder brands were added, including Godrej, M3M and Smart Homes, and exports to Europe are growing.

segments.name: Plastic profile core segment
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 13% and segment profitability rose 63%, per management. PVC profile capacity rose by 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT per annum, with utilisation around 66% in FY26.

segments.name: Aluminium windows and facade (Bangalore/Jaipur)
segments.commentary: New vertical under Mr. Varghese with INR56 crores of orders and revenue starting in Q4 FY26. Management guides INR40-50 crores of FY27 revenue; it targets EBITDA margins of about 20%.

segments.name: WPC doors and WPC wall/ceiling panels
segments.commentary: WPC door line (about INR10 crores capex) has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27. Management expects about INR15 crores of FY27 revenue; WPC wall and ceiling profile lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of about 30% revenue CAGR while sustaining EBITDA and PAT margins; management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is sustainable.
FY27 PVC profile extrusion volume growth of at least 20%; modular furniture growth of 20-25% expected.
FY27 new-capex revenue addition of INR55-60 crores, with aluminium facade INR40-50 crores and WPC doors about INR15 crores.
INR100 crores capex over FY26-FY28: about INR27 crores in FY26, INR35-40 crores in FY27 and INR20-30 crores in FY28.
Existing extrusion capacity can deliver more than INR450 crores of profile revenue at 85% utilisation; management did not give a year for reaching it.
Working capital expected to improve materially in FY27 as inventory is consumed and supplier payment cycles normalise.
capex_capacity: PVC profile extrusion capacity raised by 3,600 MT from 24,000 MT to 27,600 MT per annum in FY26; utilisation about 66%, with 80% cited as the practical benchmark.
WPC door line: machines commissioned and trials underway; commercial launch expected from Q2 FY27. WPC door capacity not yet finalised.
WPC wall and ceiling profile extrusion planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.
Aluminium windows and facade: Bangalore unit implemented; a new Jaipur factory site is under construction with capex planned in FY27. Custom fabrication, so no defined capacity.
Management expects ROE and ROCE of about 25-26% to be sustained on the new capex; it also said the new capex would earn similar returns across segments.
demand_pricing: Order book INR174 crores: UPVC windows and doors about INR84 crores, modular furniture about INR34 crores, aluminium windows and facade about INR56 crores; 100% expected to execute in 18-24 months.
Price hikes: three price revisions since the West Asia conflict began, up to 30 April. Management estimated 15-18% raw material cost inflation across its product lines.
Roughly 30% of revenue is fixed-price; B2B PVC profile distribution (over 60% of revenue) carries price revision clauses. Aluminium projects carry NALCO-linked base-price pass-through clauses.
Management said PVC resin fell from about INR115 in March to INR80-85 now; prices can move both ways.
Mobilisation advances of 10-20% of project value; net advances exceed INR7 crores versus about INR5 crores last year.
Management says WPC doors have no direct competition in India today; aluminium facade faces large international system brands and local fabricators.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the shortfall versus the 20-25% growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyers deferred supply on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and one or two in Delhi NCR. Order book was healthy and the shortfall was described as timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is a 20%+ EBITDA margin sustainable amid raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing product mix, upgraded offerings for upper-middle and high-end customers, and pre-buying of raw materials in February-March. It expects price revisions to offset the 15-18% input cost rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables fall to almost zero and inventory and receivables rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it paid suppliers in full in the last two months of FY26 to secure supply during the Middle East disruption and bought PVC resin and polymers heavily in March. Receivables rose only in line with revenue, and it expects the cycle to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 volume growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 20% volume growth in PVC profile extrusion, with new verticals adding on top. Price growth was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crores capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly internal accruals (about INR50 crores of operating cash generation in FY26), with some borrowing. Debt-to-equity is currently 0.56 and is not expected to reach 0.75.

risks_watch: Revenue timing risk: deferred project deliveries by buyers caused the FY26 shortfall against the 20-25% target.
Raw material and aluminium price volatility tied to crude oil and LME aluminium; the aluminium contracts carry base-price clauses, but UPVC and modular contracts are largely fixed-price.
Working capital: inventory build, receivables growth and near-zero payables; management guided to normalisation in FY27.
Execution of the new WPC door launch in Q2 FY27 and the aluminium facade ramp-up, including the Jaipur factory build.
The 30% CAGR target rests on new verticals with no revenue history; management has not disclosed WPC capacity figures.
Margin sustainability: management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is durable, but competitive pricing and price-cut pressure are noted in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, capex and the 30% CAGR target, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss and the working capital build. Several answers were vague on volumes, pricing and WPC capacity, and some figures were corrected during the call.
key_quotes: Q4 was our strongest quarter ever, with EBITDA margin crossing 21% and PAT growth of nearly 55% year-on-year.
Importantly, this is a matter of timing, not a loss of business, as our underlying demand remains robust.
Based on our current visibility, we are targeting approximately 30% CAGR revenue growth over the long term while maintaining sustainable EBITDA and PAT margins.
It's a cost-plus pricing, definitely it's a cost-plus pricing.

growth.why: Management guides ~30% long-term revenue CAGR and FY27 new-capex revenue of INR55-60 crores (aluminium facade INR40-50 crores, WPC doors ~INR15 crores) backed by a INR174 crore record order book and INR100 crore FY26-28 capex, but the 30% figure is long-term with no year and FY26 growth was only 12.5%, and the 20% PVC volume growth is backed by 66% utilisation and a 3,600 MT capacity addition.
